headline: Three points need Karandeep's decision before signing: a 24-month bar on any retail customer that the Client alone judges, a delay indemnity with no cap that covers delays the Client itself causes, and customer names and mobile numbers going to a vendor with no flow-down. Payment at 60 days and pay-for-accepted-work-only termination also sit outside his checklist.

findings.title: 24-month conflict-of-interest bar on any retail customer, judged by the Client alone, binding Affiliates and subcontractors; possible conflict, for counsel
findings.quote: the Supplier shall not, and shall procure that its Affiliates and subcontractors do not, undertake any project for any other customer in the retail sector where the Client considers that the project may give rise to a conflict of interest with the Client's business.
findings.explanation: The bar covers 'any other customer in the retail sector', and §7.2 makes the Client's decision on whether a conflict exists final. AtliQ already serves two retail customers in the register: Acme Retail Group (term to 9 Mar 2027) and Crestline Retail Inc. (term to 31 Jul 2027, contracted through AtliQ Inc). Both terms overlap the 3-year term in §3.1. The draft uses the word 'Affiliates' once and does not define it, and AtliQ Inc is 100% owned by AtliQ Technologies Pvt Ltd, so the bar may reach the US entity's Crestline work. Possible conflict, for counsel: whether Acme or Crestline work would be caught depends on what the Client 'considers', so the draft cannot answer it. Karandeep has cut broad bars before: he refused worldwide for three years at Al Noor and landed on GCC, term + 18 months, and he removed Europe from the CloudSpan exclusivity.

findings.title: Delay indemnity with no cap, 'howsoever caused', including delay the Client's own dependencies cause
findings.quote: arising from any delay in the delivery of any Milestone, howsoever caused, including delay attributable to the Supplier's subcontractors, third-party data providers or software vendors, or the Client's own dependencies.
findings.explanation: This is a one-way indemnity for delay of any kind, including delay the Client's own dependencies cause. §9.2 takes it outside the fees cap and §8.3 says force majeure does not excuse it. The only Client indemnity (§8.2) is for third-party IP claims. Karandeep's checklist says LDs must be capped and never open-ended, liability is 1x fees and not unlimited, and indemnity is mutual so AtliQ does not cover the other side's mistakes. At Acme he countered an open-ended delay clause with 0.5% of the milestone fee per week, capped at 5%, with no LD for client-caused delay; Northwind and Trustline ended the same way. Brightwater, signed with no exclusion for client-caused delay, produced a claim of $18,400. The exposure table shows what the recorded counter would be on M2.

findings.title: Customer names and mobile numbers go to a subcontractor with no flow-down of the Client's data terms
findings.quote: The Supplier shall comply with the Digital Personal Data Protection Act, 2023, process that data only on the Client's documented instructions, and notify the Client within forty-eight (48) hours of any personal data breach.
findings.explanation: The Client's data terms are: DPDP Act compliance, processing only on documented instructions, and a 48-hour breach notice. In the AtliQ draft with Tarang, AtliQ would hand over extracts with customer names and mobile numbers, Tarang would store them on its own systems in Chennai and may engage its own contractors. The Tarang draft contains no breach-notice duty and no instructions clause, and its confidentiality lasts 2 years against 5 years in the Client MSA. The Client's terms are therefore not passed down, and AtliQ stays responsible for subcontractors under §1.3. Karandeep's rule R-16 asks for approval and flow-down before a subcontractor touches personal data.

findings.title: Payment in 60 days is above Karandeep's 45-day maximum
findings.quote: The Client shall pay each undisputed invoice within sixty (60) days of receipt.
findings.explanation: Karandeep's checklist says payment in 30 days, 45 at most. Trustline asked for 90 and he held at 45; Brightwater's 45 days was signed without discussion. 60 days is above both. The deal is paid on three milestones, so a longer wait after each one also delays the cash needed to pay Tarang.

findings.title: Client can end for convenience in 7 days and pay only for Deliverables accepted before that date
findings.quote: On such termination the Client shall pay only for Deliverables accepted before the termination date.
findings.explanation: Karandeep's checklist says that on termination the client pays for work done. Here only the Client has the convenience right and work in progress is not paid. The Acme MSA, which he accepted, pays for services rendered and milestones completed or in progress, pro rata. With milestones months apart, a 7-day notice could leave AtliQ and Tarang unpaid for work already done.

findings.title: Tarang is proposed in Schedule 1, but §1.3 needs the Client's prior written consent and the vendor agreement is still a draft
findings.quote: The Supplier shall not subcontract any part of the Services without the Client's prior written consent.
findings.explanation: Schedule 1 says AtliQ 'proposes' Tarang for data labelling in Milestone 1. No written consent from the Client is on file, and the Tarang agreement is marked as not yet sent to the vendor. Tarang may also engage its own contractors, who are not named in the Client schedule. Karandeep has accepted consent clauses before (Al Noor §13.1), so this needs process, not a rewrite: obtain the consent in writing and make Tarang's own contractors subject to it.
